3. Both the parties filed written statements The case for the 1st party petitioner Kalu Howlader is that P. W. 2 Mazid Talukder, P. W. 3 Khaleque Talukder and P. W. 6 Abdul Barek Talukder were recorded tenants in the R.S. Khatian in respect of the disputed plot Nos. 1830, 1831, 1722 and 1724. The said recorded tenants possessed the disputed land and while in such possession they sold the western '24 acre of plot No. 1831 and western '12 acre of plot No. 1724 of the said Mouza on 15.6.69 by registered kabuliyat Ext, 1 to Kanchan Bibi, wife of 1st party petitioner Kalu Howlader and P. W. 2 Majid sold western '25 acre of Plot No. 1831 and '45 acre of plot Nos. 1722 and 18300fthe said Mouza of 27.5.60 to petitioner's wife Kanchan Bibi by a registered kabala Ext. 1/1 Since. Purchase P. W. 1 first party petitioner Kalu Howlader possesses the western '84 acre of Plot Nos. 1830 and 1831 of Mouza Purba Taikka. 

 5. The 1st party petitioner remained 6 witnesses and filed the relevant RS. Khatians Rent receipts and the two registered documents by which the disputed land was transferred by P.W. 2 Majid, P.W. 3 Khaleque and P.W. 6 Barek to Kanchan Bibi, the wife of the petitioner on behalf of the 2nd party 3 witnesses were examined. The learned Magistrate ordered that the 2nd party men are entitled to remain in possession of the disputed land until evicted therefrom in due course of law.
